claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent more than a hundred thousand years getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (read); https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (read); Crossref metadata for doi:10.1086/172103 and doi:10.1023/A:1022952621810 (bibliographic data only, no abstract); ADS abstract pages for 1992ApJ...401..759M and 2003SoPh..212....3S and the Springer page for Stix returned bot walls; neither paper is on arXiv
claims.note: The two NASA pages cited in SOURCES disagree on the side of the hook's threshold. MSFC: an individual photon 'takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer' (0.7 R), which supports >1e5 years. SVS 'Origin of Light': 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface', which contradicts it. SOURCES entry 2 sets SVS aside as 'an outreach figure with no derivation', but the MSFC page is equally an outreach page with no derivation; the only thing that breaks the tie is Mitalas & Sills (1.7e5 yr) and Stix (~3e7 yr), and SOURCES itself says those were not read at source (I could not reach them either). So on the sources actually read, a pedant can quote NASA saying 40,000 years and the hook fails A3/A4. Change one of: (a) read Mitalas & Sills 1992 (and ideally Stix 2003) at source, quote the figure as read in SOURCES entry 2, and re-run the check; or (b) narrow the hook to what both NASA pages support, e.g. 'spent more than ten thousand years getting out of the Sun' (on screen '10,000+ YEARS'), keeping the MSFC/SVS disagreement in SOURCES. If neither is possible, stop and ask the owner (F4). A4: the first sentence alone carries this claim, so it is the line that must be fixed.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?c (c = 299 792 458 m/s exact, 2022 CODATA); https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html (semimajor axis 149.598e6 km, perihelion 147.095e6 km, aphelion 152.100e6 km, eccentricity 0.0167); https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 ('Light takes eight minutes to travel the 93 million miles from the sun to Earth'); IAU 2012 Resolution B2 PDF not reachable (IAU list links to Google Drive, blocked by proxy)
claims.note: 1 AU / c = 499.0 s = 8.32 min; perihelion 8.18 min, aphelion 8.46 min, matching SOURCES' 8.2-8.5 min and +/-1.7%. 'Eight minutes' is a rounding down of 8 min 19 s, the same rounding NASA SVS uses. The IAU AU value itself was not opened, but NSSDC's semimajor axis gives the same result and SVS (cited in SOURCES entry 5) states the figure directly.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.note: Holds under either NASA figure (40,000 years or about a million years) against eight minutes, so it does not depend on how claim 1 is resolved.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.note: SVS: each photon is 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'. MSFC: radiation in the radiative zone is 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays' and the energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Both support 'not the same light' (absorbed and re-emitted, and a different kind of radiation).

claims.claim: It starts as gamma rays and leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: MSFC: the pp chain's second step produces 'a helium-3 nucleus and a gamma ray'; the reactions 'release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Supports the wording as spoken. Caveat for the author, not a blocker: MSFC describes the radiation inside as 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays', and the script's own animation note says it is still X-ray at 0.7 R; 'starts as' (origin in fusion) is what the source supports, so do not extend it to 'travels as gamma rays'.
Qualitative; true under either NASA figure (40,000 years or about a million years), so it stands whichever way claim 1 is fixed.

claims.claim: Its last eight minutes were the trip to you.
claims.note: Same figure as claim 2 (8.2-8.5 min, rounded to eight).

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES / surface to your skin / not to scale (Sun-Earth shot with a pulse crossing the gap)
claims.note: As claim 2; 'surface' matches 1 AU being measured to the photosphere-level light time. The shot is labelled not to scale, satisfying A6.

claims.claim: 100,000+ YEARS / energy, core to surface / not to scale
claims.note: Same number as claim 1, so same problem: NASA SVS gives 40,000 years to the surface and the papers that would settle it were not read at source. Change together with claim 1 (e.g. '10,000+ YEARS'), or keep it only once Mitalas & Sills is read at source and quoted in SOURCES.
Same number as claim 1; same fix (e.g. '10,000+ years getting out'), or keep only after the primary paper is read at source.

claims.claim: THE TRIP / 8 minutes to you / not to scale (back on the Sun-Earth shot)
claims.note: As claim 2; labelled not to scale.

claims.claim: Sun cutaway with rings at 0.25 R and 0.7 R (core / radiative zone / convection zone)
claims.note: MSFC: core is 'the innermost 25%'; radiative zone 'from 25% of the distance to the surface to 70%'; convection zone 'the outermost 30%' and 'from a depth of about 200,000 km' (about 0.71 R). The 0.713 R helioseismic value from Christensen-Dalsgaard et al. was not read at source (only Crossref metadata), but MSFC alone supports the 0.7 ring.

claims.claim: Random-walk path from the centre to the 0.7 ring with side-stubs (photons bouncing through the radiative zone)
claims.note: MSFC: energy 'is carried by light (photons) that bounces from particle to particle through the radiative zone'; SVS: 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly'. The walk stops at 0.7 R where MSFC switches to convection. Step size is schematic and the sequence carries a 'not to scale' label.

claims.claim: Path colour violet to pale yellow by log temperature from 15 MK (r=0), 7 MK (0.25 R), 2 MK (0.7 R), 5,700 K (surface); about 10% of the way to yellow at 0.25 R and 26% at 0.7 R
claims.note: MSFC: centre 'about 15,000,000 deg C'; radiative zone temperature 'falls from 7,000,000 deg C to about 2,000,000 deg C'; base of convection zone 'about 2,000,000 deg C'; surface '5,700 K'. (MSFC also says the core edge is 'half its central value', i.e. 7.5 MK; the 7 MK used is MSFC's own radiative-zone figure, and the difference is invisible in the colour.) Recomputed: ln(15/7)/ln(15e6/5700) = 9.7% and ln(15/2)/ln(15e6/5700) = 25.6%, matching 10% and 26%. Hue is schematic (high-energy radiation inside, visible at the surface), consistent with MSFC.

claims.claim: Rotating convection cells fill the shell from 0.7 R to the surface
claims.note: MSFC: energy moves 'by convective fluid flows (boiling motion) through the convection zone, the outermost 30%' and 'convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface'.

claims.claim: A fan of five short yellow light rays leaves the surface
claims.note: MSFC: the energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Schematic; the ray count carries no claim.
